limitation: Two bounded actual-provider trials are not a reliability, latency, or benchmark claim.
error_summary: new row for relation "agent_session_chat_tasks" violates check constraint "agent_session_chat_tasks_check"

observations.observation: The real provider returned HTTP 200 with an appropriate unconfirmed answer, but persisting agent_session_chat_tasks failed with 23514 agent_session_chat_tasks_check. The probe holds one outer transaction across both trials and maps internal transactions to SAVEPOINTs. PostgreSQL now() stays at outer transaction start while the second canonical Session is created later. Task created_at defaults to now(); its application-computed expiry can therefore exceed created_at + 30 days.
observations.missing_proof: The initial runner did not capture second Session timestamps, failed INSERT bind values, or statement_timestamp/clock_timestamp. Those exact values cannot be recovered after rollback.
observations.scope_assessment: The outer transaction shape exposes the constraint consistently; an ordinary independent Chat transaction with an already-existing Session generally avoids this particular ordering. The backend owner is independently testing an application/database clock skew case and a same-clock clamp fix. No implementation was changed by the probe owner.

observations.observation: The reply asks for the missing date/time zone but supplies the example Friday, March 15, 2025, US Eastern. Python calendar verification shows 2025-03-15 was Saturday. The example is clearly labeled e.g. and never presented as canonical screenshot evidence, but a concrete invented date is unnecessary and erroneous.
observations.suggestion: Ask the missing date/time-zone question directly. If a format example is necessary, use placeholders instead of invented dates.
